If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 11 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. -n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

The suite is correct against the spec. I re-derived the expected values by hand and found no wrong expectation. The run gave 14 passing and 4 failing, and the 4 failures are exactly the expected CR/LF `PORT` tests.

**What I checked**
- **Sort:** `[4,5,2,3,1,6]` is right. Ids 4 and 5 sort first by date and start. At 09:00 the rooms then follow the fixed order Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos (ids 2, 3, 1). Id 6 is on the next date.
- **Date filter:** the first repeated `date` wins, and `?date&date=…` gives an empty first value, so 400. `+` decodes to a space, so 400. Other params and `Date=` are ignored.
- **409:** the 09:59–11:01 request overlaps all three bookings and the 10:30–23:00 request overlaps two. Each expected message names the earliest-starting overlap. A booking starting at 12:00 after one ending at 12:00 is allowed.
- **Routing:**
  - `%2F`, `1.` and `1;x` fall under the id route, so DELETE gives 404 `booking not found` and GET gives 405.
  - Paths holding a `/`, such as `/api/bookings//` and `/api/bookings/1/`, give 404.
  - `*`, absolute targets and `#x` give 404.
  - HEAD and OPTIONS on the listed paths give 405.
- **Other cases:**
  - A `__proto__` body gives the room error.
  - Draining a 2 MB body works on every reply kind.
  - The 30-way overlapping POST gives one 201 and 29 × 409.
  - The ENOTDIR startup case gives `cannot read data file`.

**Defects**
- **Invisible characters (low risk):** the title at line 209 holds invisible Unicode (U+3000, U+FEFF) typed literally. It is unreadable and an editor can silently strip it. Use `\u3000 \uFEFF` escapes.
- **Multi-assertion tests:** several tests pack many separate cases into one loop or test, such as lines 140-158, 180-189 and 109-121. The first failure hides the rest, and each case gets no name of its own. They are all under 50 lines.
- **Missing coverage:** there is no test for the 500 `internal error` on a save failure, with the next id unchanged. There is also no restart-persistence test and no `PORT` > 65535 or port-in-use test. Those may live in the builder suites, which I did not review, so I count this as a minor gap.
- **Leftover variable (cosmetic):** `fw` at line 210 is only used once. Inline it.
- **Concurrency test (minor):** line 91 only exercises overlapping bookings. A parallel test with non-overlapping bookings would catch duplicate ids, which the spec also requires.

## GRADE
Overall: 8/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 8 — helpers are small and focused; some tests bundle many cases in one loop, which hides later failures.
naming: 9 — descriptive test and helper names (`expectError`, `boot`, `seeded`, `raw`).
duplication: 8 — shared helpers are used; the `raw(...)` plus header boilerplate repeats in a few places.
size: 9 — 224 lines; every function is well under 50 lines.
errors: 8 — nothing is swallowed and the failures are loud; it does not cover the 500 save-failure path or port-in-use.
tests: 8 — expectations are exact and correct against the spec and catch plausible wrong implementations; the 500/persistence/>65535 gaps keep it from higher.
security: 10 — no secrets; temp dirs via helper, no injection.
leftovers: 9 — no console.log or debug code; the title at line 209 holds invisible literal characters.
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-788acd71/test/final.test.mjs:209 replace the literal invisible characters with `\u3000 \uFEFF` escapes.
- /root/bench-runs/h4-788acd71/test/final.test.mjs:140-158 split into one test per id or path case (for example with `for … test(...)`) so a failure names the case.
- /root/bench-runs/h4-788acd71/test/final.test.mjs:180-189 split the date-filter assertions into separate tests for clearer failures.
- /root/bench-runs/h4-788acd71/test/final.test.mjs:210 inline the one-use `fw` variable.
- /root/bench-runs/h4-788acd71/test/final.test.mjs:43-51 add `PORT=65536` and port-in-use cases if they are not covered in the builder suites. Also add a 500 `internal error` test for a save failure with the next id unchanged, and a non-overlapping concurrent-POST id-uniqueness test near line 91.
